title: ESP tests in a Faraday cage at the Round Table

tellings.quote: built a Faraday cage there and I think you know, was one of the first people as far as I understand doing ESP tests in a in a Faraday cage

plain: Greg Malatzi, a researcher speaking on Jesse Michels's podcast, says that at the Round Table Foundation, a private research group in Rockland, Maine, in the early 1950s, a Faraday cage was built: a metal enclosure that blocks radio and electrical signals. As he understands it, someone there was one of the first to run ESP tests, meaning experiments on extrasensory perception, or sensing things without the ordinary senses, inside such a cage. The point is that any results could not be put down to ordinary radio signals.
